Q4. Differentiate between a class and an object with one suitable example.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L2 2 Marks Midterm Score: 10.0
ClassObject
A logical template or blueprint.A physical entity/instance created from a class.
Does not allocate memory when created.Allocates memory in the heap when instantiated.
Declared using the class keyword.Created using the new keyword.

Example: If Car is a class (the blueprint), then a Red Tesla Model S is an object (an actual car).

Quick Recall:

  • Class: A logical template or blueprint. vs Object: A physical entity/instance created from a class.
  • Class: Does not allocate memory when created. vs Object: Allocates memory in the heap when instantiated.
  • Class: Declared using the class keyword. vs Object: Created using the new keyword.

Q5. Define encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, and polymorphism.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L2 2 Marks Midterm Score: 10.0
  • Encapsulation: Wrapping data (variables) and code (methods) together into a single unit (class), protecting the data from outside interference.
  • Abstraction: Hiding internal implementation details and exposing only the necessary functionalities to the user.
  • Inheritance: A mechanism where a new class (child) inherits properties and behaviors from an existing class (parent), promoting code reusability.
  • Polymorphism: The ability of a single entity (method, object, or operator) to take on multiple forms and behave differently based on the context.

Quick Recall:

  • Encapsulation: Wrapping data (variables) and code (methods) together into a single unit (class), protecting the data from outside interference.
  • Abstraction: Hiding internal implementation details and exposing only the necessary functionalities to the user.
  • Inheritance: A mechanism where a new class (child) inherits properties and behaviors from an existing class (parent), promoting code reusability.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Encapsulation Abstraction Inheritance Polymorphism encapsulation abstraction

Q50. Differentiate between = = and equals() when comparing String objects with a suitable example.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L3 3 Marks Midterm Score: 10.0
  • == Operator: Compares the memory references (addresses) of two objects to see if they point to the exact same object in memory.
  • equals() Method: Compares the actual contents/values of the two objects for logical equality.
String s1 = new String("Java");
String s2 = new String("Java");

System.out.println(s1 == s2);      // false (different heap objects)
System.out.println(s1.equals(s2)); // true (same content)

Quick Recall:

  • == Operator: Compares the memory references (addresses) of two objects to see if they point to the exact same object in memory.
  • equals() Method: Compares the actual contents/values of the two objects for logical equality.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
== Operator equals Method equals comparing String String objects

Q119. Analyze the difference between overloading and overriding using a small Java example for each.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.7

Comprehensive comparison between Method Overloading and Method Overriding:

CriteriaMethod OverloadingMethod Overriding
LocationOccurs within the same class.Occurs between superclass and subclass.
Method SignatureMust differ (argument types, count, order).Must be identical (name, arguments, return type).
Binding TimeCompile-time (Static binding).Runtime (Dynamic binding).
PolymorphismCompile-time polymorphism.Runtime polymorphism.
Private/Static/FinalCan overload private, static, final methods.Cannot override private, static, or final methods.
// Overloading: same class, different parameters
class MathUtil {
    int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
    double add(double a, double b) { return a + b; }
}

// Overriding: subclass redefines parent method
class Parent { void show() { System.out.println("Parent"); } }
class Child extends Parent {
    @Override
    void show() { System.out.println("Child"); }
}

Quick Recall: Overloading is same class + different parameters (compile time); Overriding is subclass + identical signature (runtime).

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Overloading vs Overriding Compile-time vs Runtime Static binding Dynamic binding Signature comparison

Q120. Given a superclass reference that refers to a subclass object, analyze which overridden method is executed and justify your answer with code.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.7

Analysis & Architectural Justification:

When a superclass reference variable holds a subclass instance, invoking an overridden method causes the subclass's method to execute.

class Base {
    void identify() {
        System.out.println("Inside Base class identification.");
    }
}

class Derived extends Base {
    @Override
    void identify() {
        System.out.println("Inside Derived class identification.");
    }
}

public class DispatchAnalysis {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Base ref = new Derived(); // Superclass reference -> Subclass object
        ref.identify();           // Output: Inside Derived class identification.
    }
}

Justification:

  • Reference Type vs Object Type: The reference type (Base) only determines which method names are legally accessible at compile time.
  • Virtual Method Table (vtable): At runtime, the JVM inspects the object header of new Derived() on the heap to find its vtable pointer. The vtable slot for identify() points directly to Derived.identify(), executing the subclass implementation via Late Dynamic Binding.

Quick Recall: The subclass method executes because Java resolves virtual methods at runtime via the heap object's vtable (Dynamic Dispatch).

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Superclass reference Subclass object Dynamic Method Dispatch vtable Virtual Method Invocation

Q197. Demonstrate synchronized access to a shared bank account balance using a synchronized method.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.7

Concurrent manipulation of financial balances without thread synchronization causes lost updates and race conditions. The program below uses a synchronized method to enforce mutual exclusion:

class BankAccount {
    private int balance = 1000;

    // Synchronized method locks 'this' monitor object
    public synchronized void withdraw(String customer, int amount) {
        System.out.println("[" + customer + "] Checking balance... Current: $" + balance);
        if (balance >= amount) {
            try {
                // Simulate processing latency
                Thread.sleep(200);
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {}
            
            balance -= amount;
            System.out.println("[" + customer + "] Successfully withdrew $" + amount + ". Remaining: $" + balance);
        } else {
            System.out.println("[" + customer + "] Transaction REJECTED! Insufficient funds for $" + amount);
        }
    }

    public int getBalance() { return balance; }
}

public class BankSyncDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        BankAccount sharedAccount = new BankAccount();

        // Two customer threads accessing the SAME account
        Thread cust1 = new Thread(() -> sharedAccount.withdraw("Alice", 700));
        Thread cust2 = new Thread(() -> sharedAccount.withdraw("Bob", 700));

        cust1.start();
        cust2.start();
    }
}

Monitor Lock Operation: When Alice enters withdraw(), she acquires the intrinsic lock on sharedAccount. Bob is blocked in the BLOCKED state until Alice completes and exits the method, preventing double-withdrawal ($1400 withdrawn from a $1000 balance).

Mutual Exclusion Invariants & Atomicity

Without synchronized, thread interleaving creates a critical race condition: both threads read balance = 1000, pass the check, and deduct $700, reducing the balance to -$400. The synchronized keyword serializes execution: Alice acquires the monitor lock, completes the deduction, and releases the lock before Bob is permitted entry.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Two people (Alice and Bob) try to withdraw $700 from an account that only has $1,000.
  • Without synchronized, both would see $1000 and both would take $700, bankrupting the account!
  • With synchronized, Alice locks the account while withdrawing. Bob has to wait outside until she finishes, and then gets correctly rejected for insufficient funds!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
synchronized method BankAccount monitor lock race condition mutual exclusion thread safety

Q11. Describe the role of the JVM in running a Java program.

Unit I CO1 | Bloom L2 2 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) is the abstract computing machine that provides the runtime execution environment for Java applications. Its primary responsibilities include:

  • Class Loading: Loads .class files into memory via the ClassLoader subsystem.
  • Bytecode Verification: Checks bytecode instructions for safety and security violations.
  • Execution & JIT Compilation: Interprets bytecode into native machine code, optimizing hot code blocks using the Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler.
  • Automatic Memory Management: Allocates heap memory for objects and reclaims unreferenced memory via the Garbage Collector.

Quick Recall: The JVM loads class files, verifies bytecode security, executes instructions (via interpreter & JIT compiler), and manages memory via Garbage Collection.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
JVM Bytecode execution ClassLoader JIT Compiler Garbage Collection

Q31. Explain why Java is called platform independent.

Unit I CO1 | Bloom L2 2 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

Java is termed platform independent because compiled Java programs can execute on any computer architecture without source-code modification or recompilation, embodying the "Write Once, Run Anywhere" (WORA) philosophy.

This is achieved via a two-step process:

  1. The javac compiler translates source code (.java) into platform-neutral bytecode (.class).
  2. Each target platform has a platform-specific Java Virtual Machine (JVM) that reads and translates this universal bytecode into native machine instructions.

Quick Recall: Java code compiles to universal bytecode, which is run by platform-specific JVMs on Windows, Linux, or Mac without recompiling.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Platform Independent WORA Bytecode JVM javac compiler

Q73. Create a Student class with private attributes, a constructor, and getter/setter methods to demonstrate encapsulation.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

Robust Data Encapsulation with integrity validation:

class Student {
    private int rollNo;
    private String name;
    private double gpa;

    public Student(int rollNo, String name, double gpa) {
        this.rollNo = rollNo;
        this.name = name;
        setGpa(gpa); // Uses setter validation
    }

    public int getRollNo() { return rollNo; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public double getGpa() { return gpa; }

    public void setGpa(double gpa) {
        if (gpa >= 0.0 && gpa <= 10.0) {
            this.gpa = gpa;
        } else {
            System.out.println("Invalid GPA range!");
        }
    }
}

public class EncapsulationFullDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Student s = new Student(101, "Tanvi", 9.4);
        System.out.println(s.getName() + " (Roll " + s.getRollNo() + ") - GPA: " + s.getGpa());
        s.setGpa(9.8);
        System.out.println("Updated GPA: " + s.getGpa());
    }
}

Quick Recall: Private fields protected by public getters and setters with internal validation boundaries.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Encapsulation Getters and Setters Data Hiding Validation Student bean

Q105. Write a short program demonstrating dynamic binding through a superclass reference.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

Dynamic Binding (Late Binding) mechanism in Java:

class Bank {
    double getInterestRate() { return 4.0; }
}
class SBI extends Bank {
    @Override
    double getInterestRate() { return 6.5; }
}
class HDFC extends Bank {
    @Override
    double getInterestRate() { return 7.1; }
}

public class DynamicBindingDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Bank b; // Superclass reference

        b = new SBI();
        System.out.println("SBI Interest: " + b.getInterestRate() + "%"); // 6.5%

        b = new HDFC();
        System.out.println("HDFC Interest: " + b.getInterestRate() + "%"); // 7.1%
    }
}

Dynamic binding delays method resolution until runtime, executing the method of the actual object referenced.

Quick Recall: JVM decides which method to run at runtime based on the actual object on heap, not the reference variable type.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Dynamic Binding Late Binding Runtime Polymorphism Virtual Method Invocation

Q107. Consider a superclass method display() and an overridden subclass method. Predict which method runs when a superclass reference refers to a subclass object, and explain why.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

Prediction & Runtime Analysis:

When a superclass reference variable refers to a subclass object (e.g., SuperClass ref = new SubClass(); ref.display();), the subclass's overridden display() method executes.

Explanation:

  • Virtual Method Dispatch: In Java, all non-static, non-final, non-private methods are virtual by default.
  • Dynamic Binding: The compiler checks that display() exists in the superclass type definition (compile-time validation). However, at runtime, the JVM inspects the actual object type present on the Heap (SubClass) using its Method Table (vtable) and dispatches execution to that object's concrete implementation.

Quick Recall: The subclass method runs because Java uses Dynamic Method Dispatch based on the actual object on the heap, not the reference variable.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Virtual method invocation Dynamic Method Dispatch vtable Heap object type Runtime resolution

Q115. Write a program demonstrating runtime polymorphism using a Shape reference for Circle and Rectangle objects.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

Runtime Polymorphism with dynamic array dispatch:

class Shape {
    void draw() { System.out.println("Drawing generic shape"); }
}
class Circle extends Shape {
    @Override
    void draw() { System.out.println("Drawing Circle with radius and border"); }
}
class Rectangle extends Shape {
    @Override
    void draw() { System.out.println("Drawing Rectangle with 4 right angles"); }
}

public class PolyShapeDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Polymorphic array of superclass references
        Shape[] shapes = { new Circle(), new Rectangle(), new Shape() };
        for (Shape s : shapes) {
            // Dynamically dispatches to each object's respective draw() implementation
            s.draw();
        }
    }
}

Quick Recall: Shape[] shapes = { new Circle(), new Rectangle() } invokes specific draw() methods at runtime dynamically.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Runtime Polymorphism Shape reference Dynamic dispatch Polymorphic array draw()

Q160. Compare FlowLayout, BorderLayout, and GridLayout for a student registration window. Select a suitable layout for each part and justify your choice.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

Designing a professional student registration window requires an optimal compound layout combining BorderLayout, GridLayout, and FlowLayout.

Layout Manager Key Characteristics Role in Student Registration Window Design Justification
BorderLayout Divides window into 5 zones (North, South, East, West, Center). Outer regions stretch. Top-Level Frame Layout Provides clear macro-structure: Title banner pinned to NORTH, form inputs centered in CENTER, action buttons anchored to SOUTH.
GridLayout Strict rectangular matrix; forces equal cell sizes; no wrapping. Center Form Fields Panel (e.g., 4x2) Guarantees exact pairwise alignment: labels in column 0 match up flawlessly with corresponding input fields in column 1.
FlowLayout Flows components sequentially; preserves preferred component sizes. South Button Bar & North Title Keeps buttons ("Submit", "Reset", "Cancel") at natural ergonomic dimensions centered side-by-side without unnatural stretching.

Compound Architecture Implementation:

// Outer Container
Frame frame = new Frame("Student Registration Portal");
frame.setLayout(new BorderLayout(10, 10));

// North Region: Banner
Panel northPanel = new Panel(new FlowLayout());
northPanel.add(new Label("STUDENT ADMISSION PORTAL", Label.CENTER));
frame.add(northPanel, BorderLayout.NORTH);

// Center Region: Form Inputs
Panel centerPanel = new Panel(new GridLayout(3, 2, 8, 8));
centerPanel.add(new Label("Roll Number:")); centerPanel.add(new TextField(15));
centerPanel.add(new Label("Student Name:")); centerPanel.add(new TextField(15));
centerPanel.add(new Label("Department:"));   centerPanel.add(new TextField(15));
frame.add(centerPanel, BorderLayout.CENTER);

// South Region: Buttons
Panel southPanel = new Panel(new FlowLayout(FlowLayout.CENTER, 15, 10));
southPanel.add(new Button("Submit Registration"));
southPanel.add(new Button("Clear Form"));
frame.add(southPanel, BorderLayout.SOUTH);

Architectural Comparison & Layout Trade-offs

Using a compound layout strategy maximizes usability: BorderLayout manages macro-level window structure, GridLayout(3, 2) guarantees that form input boxes align symmetrically with descriptive labels, and FlowLayout preserves the ergonomic proportions of push buttons without stretching them unnaturally.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • The Big Picture (BorderLayout): Organizes the entire window into Header (North), Main Form (Center), and Buttons (South).
  • The Form (GridLayout): Perfect 2-column grid so labels neatly line up with text boxes.
  • The Buttons (FlowLayout): Keeps the "Submit" and "Reset" buttons sitting naturally side-by-side without getting stretched across the whole screen.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Compound Layout BorderLayout GridLayout FlowLayout Student Registration pairwise alignment

Q195. Create a user-defined InvalidAgeException and throw it when the entered age is below 18.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.6

User-defined (custom) exceptions enhance enterprise application architecture by creating domain-specific error types that capture business rule violations. The program below defines InvalidAgeException to enforce voting eligibility validation.

Program Implementation

// 1. Custom checked exception extending java.lang.Exception
class InvalidAgeException extends Exception {
    private int rejectedAge;

    public InvalidAgeException(String message, int age) {
        super(message); // Passes error message to Throwable
        this.rejectedAge = age;
    }

    public int getRejectedAge() {
        return rejectedAge;
    }
}

public class VoterEligibilityChecker {
    // 2. Declare custom exception in method signature using 'throws'
    public static void validateAge(int age) throws InvalidAgeException {
        if (age < 18) {
            // 3. Explicitly throw custom exception instance using 'throw'
            throw new InvalidAgeException("Voting Ineligible: Age must be 18 or older.", age);
        } else {
            System.out.println("Verification Passed: Age " + age + " is eligible to vote!");
        }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] testAges = {21, 15, 18, 12};

        for (int age : testAges) {
            System.out.println("
Validating applicant with age: " + age);
            try {
                validateAge(age);
            } catch (InvalidAgeException ex) {
                System.err.println("CUSTOM EXCEPTION CAUGHT: " + ex.getMessage());
                System.err.println("Rejected Invalid Value: " + ex.getRejectedAge() + " years old.");
            }
        }
    }
}

Design Standards for Custom Exceptions

  • Checked vs Unchecked Choice: Extending java.lang.Exception creates a checked exception, forcing callers to implement recovery logic. Extending RuntimeException creates an unchecked business exception.
  • Constructor Delegation: Invoking super(message) initializes the standard message and captures the JVM execution call stack for diagnostics.
  • Diagnostic State: Custom fields (such as rejectedAge) store the illegal data payload for logging and forensic error auditing.

Step-by-Step Execution Walkthrough

1. Custom Exception Class: InvalidAgeException extends java.lang.Exception, designating it as a checked exception that the compiler requires callers to handle.

2. Method Declaration: validateAge(int age) throws InvalidAgeException declares that this method may throw the custom exception if the business rule is violated.

3. Throwing & Catching: When age is below 18, throw new InvalidAgeException(...) halts the method and creates an exception instance with diagnostic payload. In main(), the catch block intercepts it, prints the diagnostic message via ex.getMessage(), and logs the rejected age via ex.getRejectedAge().

This ensures business domain constraints are strictly validated before processing critical operations.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Create: Write class InvalidAgeException extends Exception.
  • Check: If age < 18, blow the whistle: throw new InvalidAgeException("Too young!", age);
  • Catch: Wrap the call in try-catch (InvalidAgeException e) to display the custom error politely!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:

Q8. What is bytecode, and why is Java considered platform-independent?

Unit I CO1 | Bloom L2 2 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5

Bytecode is a highly optimized set of instructions generated by the Java compiler (javac) after compiling the source code. It is not machine code, but rather intermediate code.

Java is platform-independent because the compiler generates this bytecode instead of native machine code. This bytecode can be executed on any operating system as long as that system has a JVM (Java Virtual Machine) installed to interpret it (Write Once, Run Anywhere).

Quick Recall:

Q18. What is Garbage Collection in Java? When does an object become eligible for garbage collection?

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L2 2 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5

Garbage Collection (GC) is the process by which Java programs perform automatic memory management, freeing up the heap by deleting objects that are no longer in use.

An object becomes eligible for garbage collection when it is completely unreferenced (i.e., no live thread can access it). This happens if its reference is set to null, if it is created anonymously, or if references are reassigned.

Q31. Explain the Top-Down and Bottom-Up approaches with a suitable example.

Bottom-Up Approach: The smaller modules or objects are designed first, and then integrated together to form the complete system (used in Object-Oriented Programming like Java).
Example: Designing the engine, wheels, and doors first as independent objects, then assembling them to build the car.

Q49. Explain the two ways of creating a String in Java: using a string literal and using the new keyword.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L2 3 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5
  • String Literal: String s = "Hello";
    The JVM first checks the String Constant Pool. If "Hello" exists, it returns the reference. If not, it creates it. This is highly memory-efficient.
  • new Keyword: String s = new String("Hello");
    The JVM forces the creation of a brand new String object in the Heap memory, bypassing the pool entirely, even if "Hello" already exists in the pool.

Quick Recall:

  • String Literal: String s = "Hello";The JVM first checks the String Constant Pool. If "Hello" exists, it returns the reference. If not, it creates it. This is highly memory-efficient.

Q63. Explain Java's platform independence in detail, from source code compilation to bytecode execution through the JVM.

Unit I CO1 | Bloom L2 5 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5

Java's "Write Once, Run Anywhere" capability relies on its two-step execution process:

  1. Compilation: The developer writes Program.java (Source Code). The Java Compiler (javac) compiles this into Program.class. Instead of compiling it into machine-specific code (like C++), it compiles it into Bytecode. This bytecode is entirely independent of the underlying OS or hardware.
  2. Execution: The compiled bytecode is transported to any machine (Windows, Mac, Linux). That machine must have a JVM (Java Virtual Machine) installed. The JVM reads the bytecode and translates it into the specific machine-level instructions native to that exact operating system.

Therefore, while the JVM is platform-dependent, the Java program (bytecode) itself is totally platform-independent.

  • Compilation: The developer writes Program.java (Source Code). The Java Compiler (javac) compiles this into Program.class. Instead of compiling it into machine-specific code (like C++), it compiles it into Bytecode....
  • Execution: The compiled bytecode is transported to any machine (Windows, Mac, Linux). That machine must have a JVM (Java Virtual Machine) installed. The JVM reads the bytecode and translates it into the specific...

Q74. Explain constructor overloading and constructor chaining in Java. Compare their purpose, implementation, and execution using suitable examples involving this() and super().

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L3 5 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5

Overloading allows a class to have multiple constructors with different parameters. Chaining allows these constructors to call each other, or call the parent's constructor, to avoid duplicating initialization logic.

class Parent {
    Parent() { System.out.println("Parent init"); }
}
class Child extends Parent {
    int x, y;
    
    Child() {
        this(0, 0); // Constructor Chaining via this()
    }
    
    Child(int x, int y) { // Overloaded constructor
        super(); // Constructor Chaining via super() to Parent
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    }
}

Q76. Explain Garbage Collection and finalization in Java. Discuss different situations in which an object becomes eligible for GC, the role of finalize(), why finalize() is deprecated, and modern alternatives such as try-with-resources and Cleaner.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L2 5 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5

Garbage Collection automatically deallocates memory for objects that are no longer reachable.

  • Eligibility: An object is eligible if its reference is set to null, reassigned, or created anonymously.
  • finalize(): A method in the Object class historically called by the GC just before destroying the object to release non-Java resources.
  • Deprecation: finalize() was deprecated in Java 9 because it is unpredictable, impacts performance, and can cause memory leaks if implemented poorly.
  • Modern Alternatives: Use try-with-resources (implementing AutoCloseable) for deterministic resource cleanup, or the java.lang.ref.Cleaner API.

Q85. Explain dynamic binding in detail with a Java program using a superclass reference and subclass object. Also explain how method overriding is resolved at run time.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L3 5 Marks Midterm Score: 9.5

Dynamic Binding occurs when the compiler cannot determine the method implementation at compile time, so the JVM resolves it during execution.

class Vehicle {
    void move() { System.out.println("Moving"); }
}
class Car extends Vehicle {
    @Override
    void move() { System.out.println("Driving on wheels"); }
}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Vehicle v = new Car(); // Superclass ref, Subclass object
        v.move(); // Outputs: Driving on wheels
    }
}

At compile time, the compiler ensures move() exists in Vehicle. At runtime, the JVM notices the object is actually a Car and executes the overridden version.

Quick Recall:

  • Dynamic Binding occurs when the compiler cannot determine the method implementation at compile time, so the JVM resolves it during execution.
  • At compile time, the compiler ensures move() exists in Vehicle.

Q148. A button click does not update a label. Analyze two possible event-handling mistakes and suggest corrections.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.5

When a button click fails to update a target label in Java AWT, the root cause invariably lies in a breakdown within the Delegation Event Model. The two most prevalent mistakes are analyzed below:

Mistake 1: Forgetting to Register the Listener with the Event Source

Defect: The programmer creates the Button and defines the actionPerformed() method, but fails to call button.addActionListener(...). Because no listener is registered in the button's internal observer list, clicks generate events that are discarded silently.

// WRONG: Event generated but never dispatched
Button btn = new Button("Submit");
// Missing: btn.addActionListener(this);

// CORRECTION: Explicitly register the listener callback
btn.addActionListener(this);

Mistake 2: Variable Shadowing / Scope Re-declaration

Defect: The class declares an instance variable Label lblOutput, but the constructor re-declares a local variable Label lblOutput = new Label(). The local reference is added to the screen, while actionPerformed() modifies the unattached instance variable (or throws a NullPointerException).

public class DefectDemo extends Frame implements ActionListener {
    private Label lblOutput; // Instance field

    public DefectDemo() {
        // WRONG: 'Label' type re-declared locally, shadowing the instance field!
        Label lblOutput = new Label("Initial"); 
        add(lblOutput);
    }

    public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e) {
        // Modifies the NULL instance variable, NOT the screen component!
        lblOutput.setText("Updated!"); // Throws NullPointerException!
    }
}

// CORRECTION: Assign to instance field directly:
lblOutput = new Label("Initial");

Mistake 3: Uncaught Runtime Exceptions Inside actionPerformed

Defect: If an unhandled exception (such as NullPointerException or NumberFormatException) occurs during event handling before reaching label.setText(), the execution aborts silently on the Event Dispatch Thread without updating the screen.

Correction: Always enclose event-handling logic within robust try-catch blocks to log errors and guarantee GUI feedback.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Mistake 1: The Disconnected Doorbell. You wired the bell inside your house, but forgot to hook the button on the porch (forgot btn.addActionListener(this)). Clicks do nothing!
  • Mistake 2: The Evil Twin (Shadowing). You declared a label variable at the top of your class, but inside the constructor you typed Label lbl = ... again. You ended up changing an invisible ghost label instead of the one on screen.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
addActionListener variable shadowing Delegation Event Model NullPointerException actionPerformed

import java.awt.*;
import java.awt.event.*;

public class CourseRegistrationApp extends Frame implements ActionListener {
    private TextField txtStudentName;
    private Choice choiceCourse;
    private Button btnSubmit;
    private Label lblConfirmation;

    public CourseRegistrationApp() {
        setTitle("Student Course Registration System");
        setLayout(new GridLayout(5, 2, 10, 10));

        // Form Fields
        Label lblName = new Label("Student Full Name:");
        txtStudentName = new TextField(20);

        Label lblCourse = new Label("Select Degree Course:");
        choiceCourse = new Choice();
        choiceCourse.add("B.Tech Computer Science");
        choiceCourse.add("B.Tech Information Technology");
        choiceCourse.add("B.Tech Artificial Intelligence");
        choiceCourse.add("Master of Computer Applications");

        btnSubmit = new Button("Submit Registration");
        lblConfirmation = new Label("Please complete all fields.");

        // Wire event listener
        btnSubmit.addActionListener(this);

        // Add to grid layout
        add(lblName);
        add(txtStudentName);
        add(lblCourse);
        add(choiceCourse);
        add(new Label()); // Filler cell
        add(btnSubmit);
        add(new Label("Status:"));
        add(lblConfirmation);

        addWindowListener(new WindowAdapter() {
            public void windowClosing(WindowEvent e) {
                System.exit(0);
            }
        });

        setSize(440, 240);
        setLocationRelativeTo(null);
        setVisible(true);
    }

    @Override
    public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e) {
        String student = txtStudentName.getText().trim();
        String course = choiceCourse.getSelectedItem();

        if (student.isEmpty()) {
            lblConfirmation.setForeground(Color.RED);
            lblConfirmation.setText("Error: Name cannot be empty!");
        } else {
            lblConfirmation.setForeground(new Color(16, 185, 129)); // Green
            lblConfirmation.setText("Confirmed: " + student + " registered for " + course);
            txtStudentName.setEditable(false);
            btnSubmit.setEnabled(false);
        }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        new CourseRegistrationApp();
    }
}

Validation & Feedback Lifecycle

When the user enters their full name and selects a degree option from the dropdown menu, clicking "Submit Registration" performs validation. If the name field contains only whitespace, the label turns red with an error message. Upon valid submission, the confirmation label turns green, the text field is locked with setEditable(false), and the submit button is disabled to prevent duplicate database entries.

Q159. Analyze why an ActionListener may not respond to a button click. Identify two likely coding errors and show how to correct them.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.5

In Java's Delegation Event Model, an ActionListener failing to respond to button clicks is a classic runtime defect. Two primary coding errors and their diagnostic fixes are detailed below:

Defect 1: Missing Listener Registration (Unwired Observer)

Analysis: The button is instantiated and added to the layout, and the class implements ActionListener with a valid actionPerformed() method. However, the programmer omitted the registration statement button.addActionListener(this). The AWT EventQueue generates the ActionEvent on click, but finds an empty listener collection in the button peer, dropping the event with no error message.

// FAULTY CODE:
Button btnSubmit = new Button("Submit");
add(btnSubmit); // Button visible on screen, but deaf to clicks!

// RESOLUTION:
btnSubmit.addActionListener(this); // Registers callback with event source

Defect 2: Faulty Source or ActionCommand Filtering in actionPerformed

Analysis: In classes listening to multiple controls, actionPerformed() frequently filters events via e.getSource() or e.getActionCommand(). Comparing strings using reference equality == instead of .equals(), or comparing against the wrong button reference, causes the entire conditional block to evaluate to false silently.

// FAULTY CODE:
public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e) {
    if (e.getActionCommand() == "Submit") { // BUG: '==' checks pointer address, NOT string content!
        updateLabel();
    }
}

// RESOLUTION: Use .equals() or check object references via e.getSource():
public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e) {
    if ("Submit".equals(e.getActionCommand()) || e.getSource() == btnSubmit) {
        updateLabel();
    }
}

Diagnostic Debugging Strategies

When an action event fails to trigger, developers should place diagnostic print statements inside actionPerformed(): System.out.println("Event fired from: " + e.getActionCommand());. If this line does not print to the console when clicked, listener registration was omitted. If it prints but the GUI doesn't update, the issue lies in variable shadowing or condition logic.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Bug 1 (Unplugged Wire): You built the button and wrote the action code, but forgot btn.addActionListener(this). The button is completely unplugged!
  • Bug 2 (String Comparison Flaw): Inside actionPerformed, using e.getActionCommand() == "Submit" fails because Java strings must be compared with .equals(), not ==.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
addActionListener actionPerformed e.getSource() getActionCommand Delegation Event Model reference equality

Q176. Differentiate between checked and unchecked exceptions.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.5

The distinction between checked and unchecked exceptions forms the backbone of Java's robust exception handling architecture:

Feature Checked Exception Unchecked Exception
Hierarchy Directly inherits from java.lang.Exception (excluding RuntimeException). Inherits from java.lang.RuntimeException or java.lang.Error.
Verification Time Verified at compile-time by the javac compiler. Ignored at compile-time; evaluated at runtime.
Handling Rule Strictly mandatory: Must be enclosed in try-catch or declared with throws. Optional: Compiler does not force catching or declaring.
Root Cause External environmental conditions beyond program control (missing files, network drop). Internal programming logic bugs (null references, bad array index, divide by zero).
Examples IOException, SQLException, ClassNotFoundException. NullPointerException, ArithmeticException, IndexOutOfBoundsException.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Checked: External risks the compiler forces you to prepare for (e.g., reading a file that might not exist). You can't even compile without handling it.
  • Unchecked: Programming mistakes that happen while running (like dividing by zero or pointing to a null object). Fix your code logic to avoid them!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Checked exception Unchecked exception RuntimeException compile-time verification IOException NullPointerException

Q187. Differentiate between throw and throws.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.5

While syntactically similar, throw and throws fulfill complementary roles in Java's exception handling system:

Characteristic throw Keyword throws Keyword
Purpose Used to explicitly throw an instantiated exception object. Used to declare the types of exceptions a method might throw to its caller.
Location Inside method bodies or initializer blocks. Appended to the method signature declaration.
Syntax Followed by an instance: throw new IOException(); Followed by class names: throws IOException, SQLException
Quantity Can only throw one exception object at a time. Can declare multiple comma-separated exception classes.

In summary: throw is an action verb that launches an exception from a method body, whereas throws is an informational clause that transfers exception-handling responsibility to the caller.

Quick Revision:

  • throw: The action verb inside the method body that actually launches an exception object (throw new Exception()).
  • throws: The warning sign in the method header warning callers what exceptions could happen (void readFile() throws IOException).
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
throw vs throws method signature explicit exception exception declaration Throwable

        this.length = length;
        this.width = width;
    }

    // Method to calculate area

}

import java.awt.*;

public class CourseRadioDemo extends Frame implements ItemListener {

    private Checkbox rbJava, rbPython, rbCpp;

Q147. Compare FlowLayout and GridLayout for arranging six buttons. State which layout best matches a 2-by-3 button grid and why.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

Arranging six push buttons presents distinct structural characteristics depending on whether FlowLayout or GridLayout is employed.

Feature FlowLayout GridLayout(2, 3)
Spatial Organization Sequential row placement left-to-right; wraps dynamically based on container width. Fixed rectangular mathematical matrix divided into equal rows and columns.
Component Sizing Respects individual preferred size of each button (label length determines button width). Forces all buttons to uniform identical width and height regardless of text length.
Window Resizing Behavior Unpredictable reflow: shrinking width reorganizes 6 buttons into 1x6, 3x2, or 6x1. Maintains strict 2-row by 3-column topology; scales cells proportionally.
Gaps & Alignment Horizontal and vertical pixel gaps, aligned LEFT, CENTER, or RIGHT. Uniform horizontal and vertical pixel gaps between cells.

Conclusion & Justification:

GridLayout is unequivocally superior for a 2-by-3 button arrangement. new GridLayout(2, 3, 5, 5) guarantees a deterministic geometric matrix of exactly 2 rows and 3 columns that will never break or wrap onto stray lines during window resizing.

Layout Sizing Formula & Grid Mathematics

In GridLayout(r, c), the container calculates component bounds dynamically: cellWidth = (containerWidth - (c - 1) * hgap) / c and cellHeight = (containerHeight - (r - 1) * vgap) / r. This mathematical guarantee ensures that regardless of font sizes or label lengths, all six buttons remain perfectly symmetric, aligned, and proportional across screen resolutions.

Furthermore, FlowLayout exhibits dynamic reflow: stretching the window displays all buttons in one horizontal line (1x6), whereas narrowing it forces buttons onto multiple rows (3x2 or 6x1). Only GridLayout(2, 3) preserves the user's mental model of a structured two-row matrix.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • FlowLayout is like words on a page: if the window is wide, all 6 sit on one line; if narrow, they wrap into messy rows.
  • GridLayout(2, 3) is like an ice cube tray: exactly 2 rows and 3 columns of identical size, locked in place forever.
  • Winner for a 2x3 grid: GridLayout, because it guarantees the 2x3 shape regardless of screen size.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
FlowLayout GridLayout 2-by-3 grid preferred size wrapping uniform cells

import java.awt.*;

public class MenuBarExitDemo extends Frame implements ActionListener {

Q173. Explain the difference between start() and run().

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

The distinction between start() and run() is fundamental to multithreading in Java:

Dimension start() Method run() Method
Thread Creation Allocates a new operating system native thread and initializes a fresh private call stack. Does NOT create a new thread; executes strictly as a standard synchronous method call.
Execution Context Executes concurrently in a newly spawned separate worker thread. Executes synchronously within the context of the currently calling thread (e.g., main).
Invocation Count Can only be invoked ONCE per thread instance; subsequent calls throw IllegalThreadStateException. Can be invoked repeatedly like any ordinary Java method. 
Thread t = new Thread(() -> System.out.println("Worker"));
t.start(); // Creates new thread, executes concurrently
t.run();   // Executes synchronously in the caller thread, no new thread!

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Calling start() is like hiring a new worker: they go do the job on their own time in parallel.
  • Calling run() directly is like doing the job yourself: your current thread stops and waits for it to finish. No multithreading occurs!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
start() vs run() call stack new thread IllegalThreadStateException synchronous execution

Q189. Describe the purpose of the synchronized keyword.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

The synchronized keyword in Java provides language-level mutual exclusion (mutex) and thread safety when concurrent threads access shared resources.

Core Capabilities:

  • Monitor Lock Acquisition: Every Java object possesses an intrinsic monitor lock. When a thread enters a synchronized method or block, it acquires this lock. Any other thread attempting to access synchronized code on the same object is blocked until the lock is released.
  • Critical Section Protection: Prevents race conditions and thread interleaving during non-atomic read-modify-write sequences.
  • Memory Visibility: Enforces memory synchronization by flushing thread local CPU caches to shared RAM upon acquiring and releasing the lock.

Synchronization can be applied to instance methods, static methods (locking the class object), or synchronized statements with explicit lock objects: synchronized(lockObject) { ... } for fine-grained concurrency control.

Quick Revision:

  • synchronized puts a lock on a method or block of code.
  • Only one thread can enter and run that code at a time; all other threads must line up outside and wait.
  • It prevents data corruption when multiple threads update the same bank balance or counter.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
synchronized mutual exclusion intrinsic lock monitor critical section thread safety

Q190. Explain the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

While both ArrayList and LinkedList implement the List interface, their internal memory architectures yield radically different performance profiles:

Factor ArrayList LinkedList
Underlying Structure Dynamic resizable array (contiguous memory). Doubly-linked list (nodes with data, prev, next pointers).
Random Access (get(i)) Fast $O(1)$: Direct memory address calculation. Slow $O(n)$: Must traverse pointers from head/tail.
Insertion / Deletion Slow $O(n)$ in middle: Requires array element shifting. Fast $O(1)$ once node position is reached: Simply updates pointers.
Memory Overhead Low: Stores only elements and small reserve capacity. High: Stores two pointer references (prev, next) per element.

In practice, ArrayList is preferred for read-heavy operations with frequent indexing, while LinkedList is optimal for queue or deque implementations requiring frequent insertions and deletions at boundaries.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • ArrayList is like numbered cinema seats: instant to jump straight to seat #42, but adding someone in the middle makes everyone shift over.
  • LinkedList is like people holding hands in a chain: easy to insert a new friend into the chain, but finding person #42 requires counting down the line one by one.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
ArrayList vs LinkedList dynamic array doubly-linked list O(1) random access pointer overhead

Q192. Write a Java program that starts two threads and uses join() so the main thread waits for both to finish.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

The program below demonstrates thread lifecycle synchronization where the primary main thread spawns two concurrent worker threads and halts using join() until both workers terminate:

class WorkerService extends Thread {
    private int durationMillis;

    public WorkerService(String name, int durationMillis) {
        super(name);
        this.durationMillis = durationMillis;
    }

    @Override
    public void run() {
        System.out.println("[" + getName() + "] Task started (duration: " + durationMillis + "ms)");
        try {
            Thread.sleep(durationMillis);
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            System.err.println("[" + getName() + "] Interrupted!");
        }
        System.out.println("[" + getName() + "] Task FINISHED successfully.");
    }
}

public class ThreadJoinSynchronizationDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Main thread: Launching worker threads...");

        WorkerService workerA = new WorkerService("Worker-A", 1200);
        WorkerService workerB = new WorkerService("Worker-B", 800);

        // Start both threads concurrently
        workerA.start();
        workerB.start();

        try {
            System.out.println("Main thread: Waiting for Worker-A and Worker-B to terminate...");
            workerA.join(); // Main blocks until workerA completes
            workerB.join(); // Main blocks until workerB completes
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            System.err.println("Main thread interrupted while waiting: " + e.getMessage());
        }

        System.out.println("Main thread: All worker threads have finished. Aggregating results and exiting.");
    }
}

Synchronization Mechanics: Without join(), the main thread would print its termination statement immediately while workers were still processing in the background.

State Transition Analysis during join()

When the main thread calls workerA.join(), the JVM transitions the main thread from RUNNABLE into the WAITING state, relinquishing CPU scheduling. Once workerA completes its run() method and enters TERMINATED, the JVM notifies and resumes the main thread, which then checks workerB.join() before proceeding to final summary output.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Main thread starts two workers: Worker-A and Worker-B.
  • By calling workerA.join() and workerB.join(), the main thread stops and waits patiently.
  • Only when both workers are 100% finished does the main thread announce completion and exit cleanly.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
join() Thread thread synchronization WAITING InterruptedException WorkerService

Q196. Write a program with multiple catch blocks to handle ArithmeticException and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

The program below demonstrates multiple distinct catch blocks attached to a single guarded try region, following strict subclass-to-superclass hierarchy ordering:

public class MultiCatchDemonstration {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] data = {10, 20, 30};

        // Scenario 1: ArithmeticException trigger
        executeOperation(data, 0, 1);

        // Scenario 2: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException trigger
        executeOperation(data, 2, 8);

        // Scenario 3: Valid execution
        executeOperation(data, 2, 0);
    }

    public static void executeOperation(int[] arr, int divisor, int arrayIndex) {
        System.out.println("
--- Executing with divisor=" + divisor + ", index=" + arrayIndex + " ---");
        try {
            int value = arr[arrayIndex]; // May throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
            int result = value / divisor; // May throw ArithmeticException
            System.out.println("Computation Successful! Result: " + result);
        } catch (ArithmeticException ae) {
            System.err.println("ArithmeticException Handler: Cannot divide by zero! (" + ae.getMessage() + ")");
        } catch (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException aiobe) {
            System.err.println("ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException Handler: Invalid index " + arrayIndex + "! Array length is " + arr.length);
        } catch (Exception genericEx) {
            // General fallback handler (MUST be placed last)
            System.err.println("General Exception Handler: " + genericEx.getMessage());
        } finally {
            System.out.println("Execution cycle completed.");
        }
    }
}

Crucial Java Rule: Specific subclasses (ArithmeticException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) MUST precede broader parent classes (Exception). Reversing this order produces a compile-time error: "exception has already been caught".

Compile-Time Reachability Invariants

The Java compiler enforces strict reachability rules for multi-catch hierarchies: if a superclass handler appears before a subclass handler (e.g. placing catch (Exception e) ahead of catch (ArithmeticException ae)), compilation fails with "exception ArithmeticException has already been caught". Placing specific subclasses first guarantees correct dispatch.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • We have code that could cause two different errors: dividing by zero OR looking up a bad array slot.
  • We write two separate catch blocks: one specifically for math errors, and one specifically for bad index numbers.
  • We place a general catch (Exception e) at the bottom as a final safety net!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
multiple catch blocks ArithmeticException ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException Exception ordering try-catch-finally

Q200. Create a simple JavaBean named StudentBean with private fields, a no-argument constructor, getters, and setters.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.4

A JavaBean is a standard reusable software component adhering to three strict architectural conventions: encapsulation (private fields), public default constructor, and standardized accessor/mutator methods.

import java.io.Serializable;

// 1. JavaBean class must implement Serializable
public class StudentBean implements Serializable {
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;

    // 2. Private properties (encapsulation)
    private int studentId;
    private String studentName;
    private double cgpa;

    // 3. Mandatory public no-argument constructor
    public StudentBean() {
        this.studentId = 0;
        this.studentName = "Unknown";
        this.cgpa = 0.0;
    }

    // Optional parameterized constructor for convenient initialization
    public StudentBean(int studentId, String studentName, double cgpa) {
        this.studentId = studentId;
        this.studentName = studentName;
        this.cgpa = cgpa;
    }

    // 4. Standard Getters (Accessors) and Setters (Mutators)
    public int getStudentId() {
        return studentId;
    }
    public void setStudentId(int studentId) {
        this.studentId = studentId;
    }

    public String getStudentName() {
        return studentName;
    }
    public void setStudentName(String studentName) {
        this.studentName = studentName;
    }

    public double getCgpa() {
        return cgpa;
    }
    public void setCgpa(double cgpa) {
        this.cgpa = cgpa;
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "StudentBean [ID=" + studentId + ", Name=" + studentName + ", CGPA=" + cgpa + "]";
    }
}

Conventions Justification: The no-argument constructor enables reflection frameworks (Spring, JSP, Hibernate) to instantiate beans dynamically via Class.newInstance(); getters/setters enable automated property introspection.

JavaBeans Enterprise Framework Integration

The standard naming conventions of JavaBeans enable reflection-driven frameworks (such as Spring BeanFactory, Hibernate ORM, and Jakarta Enterprise Beans) to dynamically discover properties via java.beans.Introspector. Implementing Serializable ensures the bean can be persisted to disk or transmitted over network sockets.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • A JavaBean is like a standard blueprint for a data container:
  • 1. Variables are strictly private.
  • 2. It has an empty default constructor: public StudentBean() {} so frameworks can create it easily.
  • 3. Every variable has a pair of public get...() and set...() methods.
  • 4. It implements Serializable so its state can be saved or transmitted over a network.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
JavaBean StudentBean Serializable getters and setters no-argument constructor encapsulation

        String destination = "dest.txt";

            System.out.println("ERROR: \"" + title + "\" is already issued to another student.");

        }
    }
}

        book.issueBook();
        book.issueBook(); // Re-issue attempt fails

Q109. Analyze why checking instanceof before downcasting can prevent a ClassCastException.

Unit III CO3 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

Analysis:

In Java, the compiler permits any downcast along a valid class hierarchy (e.g., (Student) personRef) because it assumes the developer knows the runtime type. However, if personRef actually references a Teacher object on the heap, attempting to cast it to Student throws a fatal runtime ClassCastException.

// Safe pattern
if (personRef instanceof Student) {
    Student s = (Student) personRef; // Guaranteed safe
    s.study();
}

instanceof checks the runtime type metadata. If the object is not an instance of the target class (or if it is null), it evaluates to false, allowing the program to bypass the hazardous cast block.

Quick Recall: instanceof verifies the real heap object type at runtime; if it doesn't match, casting is bypassed, preventing crashes.

🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:

Q136. Create a form with a TextField and a Button that displays the entered name in a Label.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

This application implements an interactive GUI using Java AWT where a user inputs their name into a TextField, clicks a Button, and observes a personalized greeting rendered in an output Label.

Program Implementation

import java.awt.*;
import java.awt.event.*;

public class GreetingForm extends Frame implements ActionListener {
    private TextField txtName;
    private Button btnSubmit;
    private Label lblResult;

    public GreetingForm() {
        // Configure Frame window
        setTitle("User Greeting Application");
        setLayout(new FlowLayout(FlowLayout.CENTER, 15, 15));

        // Initialize UI components
        Label lblPrompt = new Label("Enter Your Name:");
        txtName = new TextField(20);
        btnSubmit = new Button("Submit");
        lblResult = new Label("Result will appear here...");

        // Register event listener
        btnSubmit.addActionListener(this);

        // Add window closing listener to handle exit
        addWindowListener(new WindowAdapter() {
            @Override
            public void windowClosing(WindowEvent we) {
                System.exit(0);
            }
        });

        // Add components to the frame container
        add(lblPrompt);
        add(txtName);
        add(btnSubmit);
        add(lblResult);

        setSize(400, 180);
        setLocationRelativeTo(null);
        setVisible(true);
    }

    @Override
    public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e) {
        String enteredName = txtName.getText().trim();
        if (enteredName.isEmpty()) {
            lblResult.setForeground(Color.RED);
            lblResult.setText("Error: Name field cannot be blank!");
        } else {
            lblResult.setForeground(new Color(16, 185, 129));
            lblResult.setText("Hello, " + enteredName + "! Welcome to Java GUI.");
        }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        new GreetingForm();
    }
}

Technical Architecture & Event Flow

  • Component Roles: TextField acts as the user data entry source, Button acts as the action event generator, and Label functions as the passive visual recipient.
  • Delegation Event Model: Calling btnSubmit.addActionListener(this) registers the enclosing class as an observer. When clicked, the Event Dispatch Thread (EDT) invokes actionPerformed().
  • Input Sanitization: The method trim() eliminates stray whitespace, preventing false submissions of empty characters.
  • Lifecycle Termination: A WindowAdapter intercepts the native OS close box click to cleanly shut down the JVM via System.exit(0).

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • The Setup: We create a text box for typing a name, a button to click, and a label for showing output.
  • The Event: When the button is clicked, actionPerformed grabs whatever text is in the box using txtName.getText().
  • The Update: It then changes the label text using lblResult.setText("Hello, " + name).

GreetingForm TextField Button Label ActionListener actionPerformed

Q142. Write a program using KeyListener to display the character typed by the user in a Label.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

The KeyListener interface intercepts hardware keyboard events. The program below captures typed characters in real time and renders them on an output label.

Program Implementation

import java.awt.*;
import java.awt.event.*;

public class RealtimeKeyMonitor extends Frame implements KeyListener {
    private TextField txtInput;
    private Label lblOutput;

    public RealtimeKeyMonitor() {
        setTitle("Real-time KeyListener Demo");
        setLayout(new GridLayout(3, 1, 10, 10));

        Label lblPrompt = new Label("Type characters in the text field below:", Label.CENTER);
        txtInput = new TextField(25);
        lblOutput = new Label("Last typed character: [None]", Label.CENTER);

        // Attach KeyListener directly to the input field
        txtInput.addKeyListener(this);

        add(lblPrompt);
        add(txtInput);
        add(lblOutput);

        addWindowListener(new WindowAdapter() {
            @Override
            public void windowClosing(WindowEvent e) {
                System.exit(0);
            }
        });

        setSize(420, 180);
        setLocationRelativeTo(null);
        setVisible(true);
    }

    @Override
    public void keyTyped(KeyEvent e) {
        char typedChar = e.getKeyChar();
        lblOutput.setText("Last typed character: '" + typedChar + "' | Unicode: " + (int)typedChar);
    }

    // Required KeyListener methods satisfied
    public void keyPressed(KeyEvent e) {}
    public void keyReleased(KeyEvent e) {}

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        new RealtimeKeyMonitor();
    }
}

Event Processing Pipeline

  • Event Flow: Pressing a key generates keyPressed, followed by keyTyped (for displayable characters), and finally keyReleased when released.
  • Character Extraction: e.getKeyChar() returns the primitive char representing the valid alphanumeric Unicode character.
  • Focus Requirement: A component must hold keyboard focus to receive KeyEvent notifications; TextField automatically gains focus when clicked.
  • KeyCode vs KeyChar: getKeyChar() returns the character typed, while getKeyCode() identifies virtual keys like Shift, Ctrl, and Arrow keys.
  • Expected Execution Behavior: Each key typed in the box immediately updates the status label showing the character and its numeric Unicode value (e.g. typing 'K' displays 'K' | Unicode: 75).

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • KeyListener listens to the physical keyboard.
  • keyTyped catches each readable character as you type.
  • e.getKeyChar() gives you the exact letter or number, and we print it right onto the label.

KeyListener keyTyped getKeyChar KeyEvent TextField input focus

import java.awt.*;
import java.awt.event.*;

public class MenuListApp extends Frame {
    private List subjectList;

    public MenuListApp() {
        setTitle("Desktop Course Catalog");
        setLayout(new FlowLayout(FlowLayout.CENTER, 20, 20));

        // 1. Build Menu Bar Hierarchy
        MenuBar menuBar = new MenuBar();
        Menu menuFile = new Menu("File");
        MenuItem itemExit = new MenuItem("Exit Application");

        // Action to terminate application when Exit is chosen
        itemExit.addActionListener(e -> {

        });

        menuBar.add(menuFile);
        setMenuBar(menuBar); // Attach menu bar to Frame container

        // 2. Build Subject List

        setLocationRelativeTo(null);
        setVisible(true);

  • Menu Component Hierarchy: MenuBar contains Menu objects, which in turn contain MenuItem instances. Menus can also contain nested sub-menus.
  • Expected Execution Behavior: The top menu bar shows 'File'. Clicking it drops down 'Exit Application'. The list displays three subjects with scrolling enabled.

Q149. Differentiate MouseListener and KeyListener and give one suitable use for each.

Unit IV CO4 | Bloom L4 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

Both MouseListener and KeyListener belong to java.awt.event, but they intercept distinct hardware peripheral interactions:

Dimension MouseListener KeyListener
Event Source Peripheral Hardware mouse/pointing device. Physical or virtual alphanumeric keyboard.
Dispatched Event Class java.awt.event.MouseEvent java.awt.event.KeyEvent
Interface Methods 5 methods: mouseClicked(), mousePressed(), mouseReleased(), mouseEntered(), mouseExited(). 3 methods: keyTyped(), keyPressed(), keyReleased().
Corresponding Adapter Class java.awt.event.MouseAdapter java.awt.event.KeyAdapter
Focus Requirement Does not require explicit input focus (triggers wherever pointer hovers/clicks). Requires the target component to possess active keyboard focus (requestFocus()).

Suitable Real-World Use Cases:

  • MouseListener: Interactive CAD/Drawing canvas where clicking captures mouse coordinates $(X, Y)$ via e.getX(), e.getY() to draw shapes.
  • KeyListener: Hotkey navigation or real-time input sanitization (e.g., blocking non-numeric keystrokes in a PIN entry field).

Code Demonstration of Listener Contracts

// MouseListener: Tracks mouse cursor coordinates and clicks
component.addMouseListener(new MouseAdapter() {
    public void mouseClicked(MouseEvent e) {
        System.out.println("Mouse clicked at X=" + e.getX() + ", Y=" + e.getY());
    }
});

// KeyListener: Captures keyboard shortcuts and Enter key submissions
component.addKeyListener(new KeyAdapter() {
    public void keyPressed(KeyEvent e) {
        if (e.getKeyCode() == KeyEvent.VK_ENTER) {
            System.out.println("Enter key shortcut triggered!");
        }
    }
});

MouseAdapter and KeyAdapter abstract classes provide empty default implementations, preventing code clutter from unused interface methods.

Adapter Pattern Utility: Because MouseListener declares five abstract methods and KeyListener declares three, implementing them directly requires writing dummy empty bodies for unused methods. Java provides MouseAdapter and KeyAdapter abstract classes which define empty implementations, enabling developers to override only the specific events they care about.

This adapter pattern greatly reduces boilerplate code in complex graphical user interfaces.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • MouseListener listens for mouse clicks and hovers (5 methods). Great for drawing apps or click-to-select maps.
  • KeyListener listens for keyboard keystrokes (3 methods). Great for shortcut hotkeys (like pressing Enter to submit) or games where arrow keys steer a character.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
MouseListener KeyListener MouseEvent KeyEvent MouseAdapter KeyAdapter

import java.awt.*;
import java.awt.event.*;

public class EnterKeyDetector extends Frame implements KeyListener {
    private TextField txtCommand;
    private Label lblStatus;

    public EnterKeyDetector() {
        setTitle("Enter Key Press Detector");
        setLayout(new GridLayout(3, 1, 8, 8));

        Label lblPrompt = new Label("Type a command and press ENTER:", Label.CENTER);
        txtCommand = new TextField(25);
        lblStatus = new Label("Status: Waiting for Enter key...", Label.CENTER);

        // Register KeyListener on the text field
        txtCommand.addKeyListener(this);

        add(lblPrompt);
        add(txtCommand);
        add(lblStatus);

        addWindowListener(new WindowAdapter() {
            public void windowClosing(WindowEvent e) {
                System.exit(0);
            }
        });

        setSize(380, 160);
        setVisible(true);
    }

    @Override
    public void keyPressed(KeyEvent e) {
        // Intercept VK_ENTER virtual key code
        if (e.getKeyCode() == KeyEvent.VK_ENTER) {
            String text = txtCommand.getText().trim();
            lblStatus.setText("ENTER Pressed! Executing command: '" + text + "'");
            txtCommand.selectAll();

    }

    public void keyReleased(KeyEvent e) {}
    public void keyTyped(KeyEvent e) {}

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        new EnterKeyDetector();
    }
}

Why keyPressed() is preferred over keyTyped(): Non-character functional keys (Enter, Esc, F1-F12, Shift, Ctrl) generate keyPressed and keyReleased with a valid e.getKeyCode(), but may not trigger keyTyped().

Virtual Key Constants & Command Execution Flow

The KeyEvent class provides virtual key constants (VK_*) representing hardware keyboard keys independent of language layout. Comparing e.getKeyCode() == KeyEvent.VK_ENTER allows instant form submission or command dispatch without requiring the user to manually click a submit button.

The Enter key also generates an ActionEvent directly on TextField components, allowing developers to choose between high-level action events or low-level key events depending on application requirements.

Q175. Explain why synchronization is used when threads share data.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

Synchronization is required when concurrent threads share mutable data to prevent race conditions and data corruption.

Technical Rationale:

  • Race Conditions: When multiple threads read and write shared variables concurrently without coordination, non-atomic operations (such as count++ which entails read, modify, and write back) interleave unpredictably, resulting in lost updates.
  • Mutual Exclusion (Mutex): Synchronization guarantees that only one thread can execute a critical section at any given instant by enforcing exclusive lock acquisition on the target object's monitor.
  • Memory Visibility: Enforces a "happens-before" relationship, guaranteeing that changes written by one thread are flushed to main RAM and immediately visible to other threads.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Imagine two people sharing a single bank card trying to withdraw money at two ATMs at the exact same second.
  • Without synchronization, both might see $100 and withdraw it, leaving the bank in the red.
  • Synchronization acts like a restroom door lock: only one person can enter at a time. Everyone else must wait until the door unlocks!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
Synchronization race condition mutual exclusion critical section happens-before data corruption

The following program intercepts an illegal arithmetic division by zero using structured try-catch-finally blocks:

public class DivisionByZeroHandling {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int numerator = 50;
        int denominator = 0;

        try {
            System.out.println("Attempting division: " + numerator + " / " + denominator);
            int result = numerator / denominator; // Triggers ArithmeticException
            System.out.println("Result: " + result);
        } catch (ArithmeticException e) {
            System.err.println("Exception Caught: Division by zero is undefined! (" + e.getMessage() + ")");
        } finally {
            System.out.println("Finally block executed: Math operations finalized and resources closed.");
        }
        System.out.println("Program resumed normal execution.");
    }
}

When denominator is 0, the JVM instantiates and throws an ArithmeticException, bypassing the second print in try, jumping into catch, and finally executing the mandatory cleanup block.

Quick Revision:

  • try attempts 50 / 0.
  • catch (ArithmeticException e) intercepts the crash and prints a friendly error message.
  • finally always runs at the end to guarantee cleanup.

Q186. Describe why the join() method is used in multithreaded programs.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

The join() method in java.lang.Thread is used to achieve thread synchronization and deterministic execution ordering.

Why It Is Used:

  • Dependency Coordination: When a master thread (e.g. main) spawns background worker threads to perform calculations or fetch data, it cannot process the final results until those workers finish.
  • Execution Blocking: Invoking workerThread.join() forces the current thread to pause execution and enter the WAITING state until workerThread completely terminates.
  • Eliminates Race Conditions: Guarantees that asynchronous tasks complete in deterministic sequence without inefficient busy-waiting loops.
Thread worker = new Thread(() -> computeResults());
worker.start();
worker.join(); // Main thread pauses until worker terminates
printSummary(); // Safe to use worker's output!

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • Think of join() as saying: "Wait for me!"
  • If the boss thread sends two workers to get coffee and donuts, it calls worker.join() so it waits for them to return before starting the meeting.
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
join() thread coordination WAITING state deterministic execution thread synchronization

Q188. Explain why multiple catch blocks may be used with one try block.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L2 3 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

Multiple catch blocks are associated with a single try block to provide specialized, granular recovery handling for diverse exception types that could arise within a complex block of code.

Key Principles:

  • Differentiated Recovery: A file processing block might throw FileNotFoundException (requiring a file-chooser prompt), NumberFormatException (requiring default value substitution), or SQLException (triggering a transaction rollback). Separate catch blocks permit distinct recovery logic for each.
  • Subclass-to-Superclass Ordering Rule: Catch blocks are evaluated sequentially from top to bottom. Specific subclass exceptions must precede broader superclasses (e.g., ArithmeticException must appear before Exception); otherwise, the compiler flags unreachable code.

Java 7 introduced multi-catch syntax (e.g. catch (ArithmeticException | ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e)) to handle multiple independent exceptions with identical recovery logic without code duplication.

Quick Revision:

Q198. Use HashMap to store subject codes and subject names, then search for and display one subject by its code.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

A java.util.HashMap associates unique keys with values using hash table indexing. The following program indexes subject codes and performs $O(1)$ fast lookups:

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Scanner;

public class SubjectCatalogLookup {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // 1. Create HashMap: Key = Course Code (String), Value = Course Name (String)
        HashMap courseCatalog = new HashMap<>();

        // 2. Populate subject mappings
        courseCatalog.put("26UITU030005", "Operating Systems");
        courseCatalog.put("26UITU030006", "Object Oriented Programming with Java");
        courseCatalog.put("26UITU030007", "Database Management Systems");
        courseCatalog.put("26UITU030008", "Design and Analysis of Algorithms");
        courseCatalog.put("26UITU030009", "Discrete Mathematics");

        System.out.println("Total courses indexed: " + courseCatalog.size());

        // 3. Search and display subjects by code
        String searchCode = "26UITU030006";
        searchSubject(courseCatalog, searchCode);

        // Search for a non-existent code
        searchSubject(courseCatalog, "INVALID_CODE_99");
    }

    public static void searchSubject(HashMap map, String code) {
        System.out.println("
Querying Catalog for Subject Code: [" + code + "]");
        // Fast O(1) containment check
        if (map.containsKey(code)) {
            String subjectName = map.get(code);
            System.out.println(" MATCH FOUND: Code " + code + " -> " + subjectName);
        } else {
            System.err.println(" NOT FOUND: Subject code '" + code + "' does not exist in catalog.");
        }
    }
}

Technical Mechanics: containsKey() computes the hash of the search key to pinpoint the specific bucket index, achieving constant-time $O(1)$ search performance.

Internal Hash Table Mechanics & Complexity

When courseCatalog.get(code) is called, the JVM computes the hash code of the string key via hashCode() and maps it to a hash bucket index via modulo arithmetic. In the absence of hash collisions, retrieval executes in constant $O(1)$ time, vastly outperforming linear search on lists.

Additionally, getOrDefault(key, defaultValue) avoids null pointer risks by returning a predefined fallback if the course code is missing.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • A HashMap is like a phonebook: give it a course code (the key), and it immediately returns the subject name (the value).
  • map.containsKey(code) checks if the course exists.
  • map.get(code) retrieves the subject title in $O(1)$ instant time!
🎯 Evaluator Scoring Keywords:
HashMap containsKey() get() subject code hash table lookup java.util.HashMap

Q199. Write a Java program using InetAddress to obtain and display both the host name and IP address of a given host.

Unit V CO5 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.3

The java.net.InetAddress class encapsulates both high-level domain hostnames and their underlying IP addresses (IPv4 / IPv6). The program below resolves remote and local network identities:

import java.net.InetAddress;
import java.net.UnknownHostException;

public class NetworkHostResolver {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String targetDomain = "www.google.com";

        // 1. Resolve Remote Host
        try {
            System.out.println("Resolving remote domain: " + targetDomain + "...");
            InetAddress remoteHost = InetAddress.getByName(targetDomain);

            System.out.println("--- Remote Host Details ---");
            System.out.println("Canonical Host Name : " + remoteHost.getCanonicalHostName());
            System.out.println("Resolved Host Name  : " + remoteHost.getHostName());
            System.out.println("IP Address String   : " + remoteHost.getHostAddress());

            // 2. Resolve Local Machine Information
            InetAddress localMachine = InetAddress.getLocalHost();
            System.out.println("
--- Local Machine Details ---");
            System.out.println("Local Host Name     : " + localMachine.getHostName());
            System.out.println("Local IP Address    : " + localMachine.getHostAddress());

        } catch (UnknownHostException uhe) {
            System.err.println("DNS Resolution Failure: Host could not be located -> " + uhe.getMessage());
        }
    }
}

Networking Lifecycle:

  • InetAddress.getByName(host) performs an asynchronous DNS lookup via native OS resolver APIs.
  • If the hostname cannot be mapped to an IP address, it throws the checked UnknownHostException.
  • getHostAddress() returns the dotted-quad textual IP representation.

DNS Resolution & Network Protocol Integration

InetAddress interfaces with underlying operating system socket libraries and DNS servers. When getByName() resolves a domain, it queries local hosts files and configured DNS resolvers. In enterprise network programming, InetAddress instances are passed directly to Socket and ServerSocket constructors for TCP/IP network communication.

The method isReachable(timeoutMillis) sends ICMP echo requests (or establishes a TCP connection on port 7) to verify if the remote host is currently reachable over the network.

ELI5 Breakdown:

  • InetAddress is Java's network phonebook.
  • You pass it a website name like "www.google.com".
  • getHostAddress() asks DNS to find the computer's actual numeric IP address (e.g., 142.250.190.46), while getLocalHost() reveals your own computer's IP!

InetAddress getByName getHostName getHostAddress getLocalHost UnknownHostException

Q69. Create a class Circle with a method to calculate area and another to calculate circumference, using Math.PI.

Unit II CO2 | Bloom L3 5 Marks End Term Score: 9.2

Geometry calculations using high-precision Math.PI:

class Circle {
    private double radius;

    public Circle(double radius) {
        this.radius = radius;
    }

    // Area = pi * r^2
    public double calculateArea() {
        return Math.PI * radius * radius;
    }

    // Circumference = 2 * pi * r
    public double calculateCircumference() {
        return 2 * Math.PI * radius;
    }
}

public class CircleDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Circle c = new Circle(7.0);
        System.out.printf("Area: %.2f%n", c.calculateArea());           // 153.94
        System.out.printf("Circumference: %.2f%n", c.calculateCircumference()); // 43.98
    }
}

Quick Recall: Area $= \pi r^2$, Circumference $= 2\pi r$, using constant Math.PI.
